title: Layout performance on dense graphs (300 nodes / ~600 edges takes ~29 s)
description: PR #16 review measured main's layout() on a dense 300-node, 593-edge graph (chain plus fan-in from 7 hubs, no instances) at ~29 s, and ~22 s with 10 instances. SPEC 'Layout' assumes ELK is fast enough for a few hundred nodes; svl-bwv.4 re-lays out while streaming. Investigate ELK options (e.g. crossingMinimization thoroughness, cycle breaking, layered.compaction, mergeEdges, separateConnectedComponents), hierarchyHandling INCLUDE_CHILDREN cost, and a size-based degradation (e.g. simpler options above N nodes/edges, or collapsing wires with many uses). Add a benchmark test with dense shapes.
acceptance_criteria: Dense 300-node/600-edge graph lays out in < 2 s in vitest (warm), with and without instances; determinism and existing geometric tests still pass; chosen options documented in CONTRACTS section 8.

title: Pyodide worker and RuntimeClient: load, run, stream, stop, restart
description:
Implement packages/web/src/runtime/worker.ts and client.ts exactly as CONTRACTS.md section 7, and wire them into the store (run/stop, runtime state, progress).

- Worker: self-hosted Pyodide from /pyodide/, progress messages per phase, load numpy/pandas/scipy/scikit-learn in the background on page open, write python/machines/**/*.py and datasets (fetched from /datasets/), install hooks, `ready` with versions. Per run: reset_between_runs, loadPackagesFromImports(source), machines.run with emit -> postMessage (toJs with dict_converter), currentCall SAB via on_enter/on_exit when isolated. `file` messages write to /home/pyodide and reply fileWritten with row count for CSVs.
- Client: createAssembler per run, onUpdate at most once per animation frame, stop(): interrupt buffer (SIGINT=2) when isolated; if no `done` within 2 s, or not isolated, terminate() + new worker + finish('stopped') from the assembler; wall_ms timeout via the same path with 'timeout'; restart(); state transitions loading -> ready -> running -> ready/restarting.
- Store: run() reads source + config, sets running/elapsedMs, writes log; Run/Stop button + elapsed counter after 2 s in the toolbar; status line shows progress and versions.
- Verify the CSP in _headers works with Pyodide (wasm-unsafe-eval vs unsafe-eval) and record the answer in CONTRACTS.md section 11.

Tests: vitest for client logic with a fake Worker (stop escalation timing with fake timers, timeout status, stale runId ignored, restart). Manual/browser: run golden_split.py from the page and see a log in the store (a temporary debug JSON view is fine; remove it before merge or hide it behind ?debug).
design:
Read first: CLAUDE.md (Working a bead), then SPEC.md 'Architecture' (all bullets), 'Hard limits', CONTRACTS.md sections 6, 7, 11.

Owns: packages/web/src/runtime/worker.ts, runtime/client.ts (+ tests), the run/stop/runtime parts of store.ts, toolbar Run/Stop.
Known pitfalls: Vite worker bundling (`new Worker(new URL('./runtime/worker.ts', import.meta.url), { type: 'module' })`); Pyodide's interrupt buffer must be set before running; KeyboardInterrupt can be swallowed by a student's bare except — the 2 s terminate fallback covers it (test with `while True:\n try: pass\n except: pass`).
Out of scope: service worker caching, measurements.
acceptance_criteria: In Chrome, Firefox and Safari (or say which were unavailable): page loads with progress, Run on golden_split.py produces a log with status ok; Stop on `while True: pass` returns within 2 s with status stopped and the page stays usable; a 2 s `time.sleep`-free busy loop past wall_ms (set wall_ms low for the test) gives timeout; the bare-except loop is killed via terminate and the next Run works. Client unit tests pass.

title: Graph builder: EventLog -> GraphModel
description:
Implement `buildGraph(log, { expanded })` in packages/log/src/graph.ts exactly as CONTRACTS.md section 8 and SPEC 'Graph construction', 'Loops and repeated calls'.

Table-driven tests from small hand-written logs (one per rule):
- function event -> call node with in-ports (type + param), const ports written as `param = text`, label inputs on the port, out-ports with bound names
- constructor -> instance node with params; method events on it -> call nodes parented to the instance, one per call site (scaler.transform on train and test = two boxes); owner not a port
- make_pipeline-style function returning a machine -> function node + instance node with createdBy
- data method (df.dropna()) -> call node with a `self` port
- machine passed as an argument -> edge from instance border
- returns_self -> no out-port; mutates on data -> changedInPlace out-port; mutates on owner -> instance versions
- expr nodes dashed, dropped when they reach no machine (transitively)
- store nodes; source nodes for tokens with no producer (and for version bumps with no event)
- same merge_key -> one node with executions sorted, slot execution included, count from the latest
- name labels: bound name in scope 0; X = X.drop(...) gives `X′` on the superseded wire
- interrupted and error executions carry through
- >300 nodes -> truncated by order with tooMany
- determinism and stable ids: building twice, and building from a log of the same program with one unrelated line changed, keeps ids of unchanged nodes.
design:
Read first: CLAUDE.md (Working a bead), then SPEC.md 'Graph model and rendering' (Machines and data, Graph construction, Loops), CONTRACTS.md sections 2 and 8 (GraphModel), 10.

Owns: packages/log/src/graph.ts (+ tests). Pure: no DOM, no ELK.
If a SPEC rule is ambiguous, decide, document it in CONTRACTS.md section 8 in the same commit, and say so in the PR.
Out of scope: expansion of student functions (M4) — accept `expanded` and ignore it.
acceptance_criteria: All rule tests pass; buildGraph on a 5,000-event synthetic log runs in < 200 ms in vitest.
close_reason: Merged PR #9 after review fixes. buildGraph(log,{expanded}) in packages/log/src/graph.ts. Method boxes per (merge key, owner instance), id n:<h>@<instance>; Execution.owner added. Only call nodes have ports; other nodes use port:null (ELK: node border). Self-edges occur (x = g(x) in a loop) — layout must handle them. Ports ordered by first appearance; out:<k>, out:mut:<param>. Instances: createdAt + versions{i,token}; ret not stored (read from log). Source nodes have no executions; show when a consumer is visible. order = line*100000+col, sources consumer-0.5. Lazy-instance/multi-output ids less stable. For q3a.6: verify self-in-inputs for data methods, loop bindings, fit mutates on real logs.

title: Event log types, worker messages and assembler
description:
Implement packages/log/src/types.ts, messages.ts and assemble.ts exactly as CONTRACTS.md sections 2 and 7.

Assembler rules that must each have a test (hand-written message sequences):
- events arrive in batches out of start order (an outer call finishes after inner ones) and the log is sorted by i
- a slot event replaces the previous slot for its merge_key, not a non-slot event
- open stubs persist until the finished event arrives; finish('timeout'|'stopped') converts remaining stubs and the currentCall entry into interrupted events
- values/bindings/output merge across batches; bindings land in the right scope
- messages for an older runId are ignored
- snapshot() during a run is a valid EventLog (status 'ok' placeholder until done)
Also export a `validateLog(x): EventLog` runtime check (hand-written, no new deps) used by tests to load fixture JSON.
design:
Read first: CLAUDE.md (Working a bead), then CONTRACTS.md sections 2 and 7.

Owns: packages/log/src/types.ts, messages.ts, assemble.ts (+ tests), exports in index.ts.
The cross-check against fixtures/streams is in the golden-graphs bead (streams may not exist yet).
Out of scope: graph building.
acceptance_criteria: All listed tests pass; types compile under strict; no runtime dependencies added.
close_reason: Merged PR #2 after review fixes. CONTRACTS §7: createAssembler(runId?), finish(status?, currentCall?); batch bindings carry optional slot_key 'b<site>.<name>' past per_site (recorder must set it, §4 + deviation 18); open replaces stub map each batch; snapshot returns done status after done; currentCall recovers only innermost call (kind function, name=func_text); client calls finish('error') with a RunError on crash. validateLog does not check per-origin required fields.

title: Golden logs, fixture streams and transparency tests
description:
Generate and check in expected logs and streams for every fixture program, and add the transparency suite.

- `python/machines/tools/gen_fixtures.py` (`pnpm fixtures`): for each fixtures/programs/*.py, write fixtures/logs/<name>.json (record()) and fixtures/streams/<name>.jsonl (every message run() emitted, one per line, with flush timing forced so batches are deterministic — e.g. a config/test hook that flushes every N events instead of by time). Pretty-printed, sorted keys, stable.
- python/tests/test_golden.py: re-records each program and compares to the checked-in log; on mismatch prints a readable diff. Assert per edge-case row the property the fixture's header comment states (e.g. edge_literals: no token appears as both an output of one event and an input of an unrelated one; edge_gridsearch: the original estimator's version never changes).
- python/tests/test_transparency.py: each fixture program run plain vs via runtime.run gives identical stdout, identical exception type/message, and identical final namespace (compare scalars by repr, arrays/frames by shape+hash, estimators by get_params + fitted attr names).
- Review every generated log by eye against SPEC's 'Edge cases and limits' table and list in the PR any row whose log looks wrong (file a follow-up rather than silently accepting).

title: Runtime: run()/record(), output capture, warnings, tracebacks, matplotlib hook
description:
Implement python/machines/runtime.py, tracebacks.py and mpl.py as CONTRACTS.md section 6, so that the worker and the tests have one entry point.

- `run(source, config, emit, on_enter=, on_exit=)`: instrument, compile as `<student>` with linecache, fresh `__main__` namespace, install recorder, capture stdout/stderr per event, warnings to `warning` entries with the student line, input() error, doubled recursion limit, then emit `done` with status ok/error and RunError (student traceback). SyntaxError path emits started(sites=[]) + done(error) and runs nothing. KeyboardInterrupt (from Pyodide's interrupt buffer) closes open events as interrupted and ends with status 'stopped' (the client may override to 'timeout').
- `record(source, config=None) -> dict`: run() with an in-memory assembler; the returned log equals Recorder.log().
- `reset_between_runs()`.
- tracebacks.student_traceback: student frames with text, recorder frames removed, library frames folded.
- mpl.py: Agg backend forced when matplotlib is imported during a run; plt.show() emits figure entries and closes figures. Imported lazily; nothing loads matplotlib unless the student does.

Tests: output tagging by event (print between two calls is tagged with the first), warning attribution line, input() message, traceback for edge_error.py has only student frames + one folded library entry with the right line, syntax error, recursion: a student recursive function depth 400 works when it works in plain CPython, KeyboardInterrupt raised from a hook mid-run gives status stopped with an interrupted event, figure entry for edge_mpl.py (PNG decodes, non-zero size), two consecutive runs share no state (pandas option set in run 1 is reset in run 2; tokens restart at v0).

title: Recorder: hooks, events, filtering, caps, streaming
description:
Implement python/machines/recorder.py exactly as CONTRACTS.md section 4, on top of transform.py and values.py. This is the heart of the project: SPEC's goals 'same behaviour as uninstrumented Python' and 'never draw a wire that isn't real dataflow' are this bead's acceptance bar.

- `__rec__`, `__bind__`, `__store__` (and pass-through `__scope__`, `__ret__`), installed in builtins with positional-only leading params, passing through when no Recorder is active.
- call filtering + fast path; kind detection incl. classmethods; signature binding with cache and arg0 fallback; data-method `self` input; inputs per origin with scalar identity guard and label-on-port values; outputs with unpack split and returns_self; mutates for owner, inputs and estimators reachable via get_params(deep=True)
- expr events (incl. hidden-call and past-cap fallback for `call` origins) recorded before their consumer; store events with forced bump
- module-scope bindings (scope 0) with per-site cap; `merge_key = "s<site>"`; count; per-site slot replacement; max_events -> status limit and recording stops while the code keeps running
- errors on innermost event, propagated on enclosing, handled flag when execution continues
- re-entry flag around all summarizing/fingerprinting/get_params; degrade-to-pass-through with diagnostics on internal errors
- streaming: batches per CONTRACTS.md section 7 ('batch' message shape, `open` stack), 100 ms flush check at hook entry, on_enter/on_exit callbacks
- `Recorder.log()` assembles the full EventLog (used by runtime.record).

Tests (python/tests/test_recorder.py) drive small inline programs through instrument + Recorder with a minimal exec helper (runtime.py is the next bead) and assert on the log. Cover at least: SPEC example (train_test_split -> 4 outputs with names), fit returns_self + mutates, chained fit().predict() owner, dropna(inplace=True) version bump, df['c']=v store, equal literals never share a token, np.bool_ results never share a token, models['rf'].fit owner identity, GridSearchCV original stays unfitted, kwargs named site/fn, super() in a class body method called from module level, student __repr__ not recorded, ufunc arg0 labels, a 30-iteration loop (20 full + slot, count 30), max_events limit, an exception inside a library call (error + re-raise identical), a deliberately broken summary (monkeypatched to raise) -> diagnostics and the program still runs.

Tracebacks: student_traceback should merge the hook/eval frames; tracebacks printed by student code still show recorder frames (documented). Recursion headroom ~4 frames shorter. title: Value table: tokens, scalar classification, fingerprints, summaries
description:
Implement `ValueTable` in python/machines/values.py exactly as CONTRACTS.md section 5.

Must each have a test:
- reference objects get `v<n>.<ver>` with n in first-seen order; same object -> same token; a dead weakref-able object's reused id() gets a new n (force with a loop creating/destroying DataFrames)
- non-weakref-able references (list, dict, tuple of non-scalars) are kept alive until reset
- classification: int/float/bool/str/bytes/None/complex, np.int64, np.float64, np.bool_ (np.True_ is a singleton), pd.NA, pd.NaT, pd.Timestamp, all-scalar tuples and frozensets -> scalar; functions, builtins, ufuncs, classes, modules -> label; DataFrame/array/estimator/list -> reference
- fingerprints: dropna(inplace=True), sort_values(inplace=True), df['c']=..., arr[0]=..., estimator fit (attribute identity changes), list.append all bump the version; reading without change doesn't; a 200,000-cell frame with a same-shape content change does not bump (documented limit); hashing falls back when cells are unhashable (lists in cells)
- `bump` always bumps
- `is_machine`: sklearn estimators, a class defined in `__main__`, a configured class; DataFrame is not
- summaries match CONTRACTS.md section 2 ValueSummary for DF (columns, dtypes, 5x8 table preview, index), Series, ndarray (1-D and 2-D), scipy sparse, scalars (repr <= 40 chars), list/dict/tuple ('list[3]'), estimators (attrs: params + fitted attrs, machine: true)
- preview budget: after 1 MB of previews, new summaries keep type/shape but omit preview
- summarize/fingerprint never triggers a student `__repr__`/property side effect visible in output (they run, but the table exposes a `reentry` context manager the recorder uses; test the manager sets/clears the flag even on exception)
- determinism: summarizing the same program's values twice gives identical JSON.

title: Transformer: Instrument rewrite and site table
description:
Implement `instrument(source) -> Instrumented` in python/machines/transform.py exactly as CONTRACTS.md section 3 (the M1-3 rules: module and class bodies only, function and lambda bodies untouched).

Rules that must each have a test (assert on `ast.unparse` of the result and on the site dicts):
- every Call outside function bodies becomes `__rec__(site, func, ...)`, nested calls wrapped first, arg order preserved, `*a`/`**k` preserved, origins after a starred arg are `unknown`
- bare-name calls to super/locals/globals/vars/dir/eval/exec/breakpoint are not wrapped (their arguments are)
- decorators are visited; def/async def/lambda bodies are not; generator functions untouched
- Assign/AugAssign/AnnAssign/for/with targets at module level produce `__bind__` with flattened Name targets; subscript/attribute targets with a Name root produce `__store__(site, root)`; class-body statements get neither
- origins: const (including -1 and all-const tuple/list/dict literals), name, call (with inner site id), expr with `reads` (names only, not lambda params or comprehension targets)
- `unpack` set for `a, b, c, d = f(...)` and not for `a, *b = f(...)` or nested targets
- site positions are code-point columns (test with a non-ASCII string literal before the call) and `text` is the exact source slice
- SyntaxError is raised unchanged
- the rewritten tree compiles and, with pass-through hooks installed in builtins, every fixture program produces the same stdout as the original (a cheap transparency check that doesn't need the recorder).

title: Assembler: currentCall dropped when it is an outer call with finished inner events
description: From PR #13 review: on a kill, the currentCall buffer holds the innermost *open* recorded call. If that is an outer call whose inner calls already finished (and were flushed), currentCall.i is lower than those events' i, so assemble.ts finish() ('currentCall.i > maxI') drops it and the interrupted call disappears. Fix: add the interrupted event when no event or stub with that i exists, regardless of maxI. packages/log/src/assemble.ts + test; CONTRACTS section 7 wording.
